figures.title: Two developmental partners in the kidney
figures.alt: Flowchart distinguishing ureteric-bud derivatives in the collecting system from metanephric mesenchyme forming the nephron epithelium.
figures.caption: Trace the two renal origins: ureteric bud to collecting system; metanephric mesenchyme to nephron epithelium. Their interaction is reciprocal. figures.title: Tongue sensation and taste
figures.alt: Tongue map showing anterior general sensation through V3, anterior taste through VII, posterior sensation and taste through IX, and epiglottic-region input through X.
figures.caption: Separate general sensation from taste. Most anterior two-thirds general sensation travels in the lingual nerve (V3), while taste travels through chorda tympani (VII). Circumvallate papillae are the IX exception despite lying anterior to the sulcus terminalis. Motor supply is not shown.

figures.title: An action potential and changing conductance
figures.alt: Aligned graphs show a neuronal action potential, an early increase in relative sodium conductance and a later, longer potassium conductance increase.
figures.caption: Read the two panels together: rapid sodium-channel activation accompanies the upstroke; sodium inactivation and delayed potassium-channel activation support repolarisation. Voltages, timing and conductances are illustrative and vary between cells. This neuronal waveform is not a universal muscle or pacemaker waveform.

figures.title: Conducting airways and gas-exchanging alveoli
figures.alt: Conducting airways are coloured red, alveoli blue; an inset shows surrounding capillaries and a conceptual oxygen and nitrogen washout graph.
figures.caption: The conducting zone carries gas; gas exchange begins in the respiratory zone. In the source’s washout key, horizontal position means exhaled volume and vertical position means relative gas concentration. The solid red oxygen-rich signal falls while the dashed blue nitrogen signal rises after breathing oxygen. The graph is qualitative, without calibrated axes; do not use it to calculate dead-space volume.
